stem: In New York, at least how far before a turn must you signal?
choices: 100 feet
50 feet
25 feet
500 feet
oneLineConcept: Signal at least 100 feet before turning
explanation:
New York law requires you to **signal at least 100 feet before you turn or change lanes**. This gives other drivers and pedestrians time to react.

**Wrong choices**
- 50 feet: 50 feet is too short. New York law requires at least 100 feet.
- 25 feet: 25 feet gives other drivers far too little warning.
- 500 feet: You may signal earlier, but the minimum is 100 feet.

stem: A fire truck with its siren and red lights on is coming toward you from behind. What should you do?
choices: Speed up to stay ahead of it
Stop right where you are in your lane
Pull over to the left side of the road
Pull over to the right edge of the road and stop
oneLineConcept: Emergency vehicle: pull right and stop
explanation:
When an **emergency vehicle with a siren and flashing lights** approaches, **pull over to the right edge of the road and stop**. Wait until it has passed before moving again.

**Wrong choices**
- Speed up to stay ahead of it: Speeding up is dangerous. Let the emergency vehicle pass.
- Stop right where you are in your lane: Stopping in the lane can block it. Pull to the right first.
- Pull over to the left side of the road: Pull to the right unless an officer tells you otherwise.

stem: You are turning left at an intersection with a green light (not a green arrow). Whom must you yield to?
choices: No one, because the light is green
Only vehicles behind you
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians crossing
Only buses and trucks
oneLineConcept: Left turn on green: yield to oncoming and walkers
explanation:
When **turning left**, you must **yield to oncoming vehicles and to pedestrians** in the crosswalk. Wait in your lane until there is a safe gap.

**Wrong choices**
- No one, because the light is green: A green light does not give a left-turning driver the right of way over oncoming traffic.
- Only vehicles behind you: Vehicles behind you are not the ones you yield to when turning.
- Only buses and trucks: You must yield to all oncoming traffic, not only large vehicles.

stem: You and another driver reach an intersection with no signs or signals at the same time. The other car is on your right. Who should go first?
choices: You, because the car is on your right
The car on your right
The faster car
The car with more passengers
oneLineConcept: Same time, no signs: yield to the right
explanation:
At an intersection **without signs or signals**, if two vehicles arrive **at the same time**, the **driver on the left yields to the driver on the right**.

**Wrong choices**
- You, because the car is on your right: It is the other way around. The driver on the left yields.
- The faster car: Speed never decides the right of way.
- The car with more passengers: The number of passengers does not matter.

stem: Your light is green and you want to turn right. A pedestrian is crossing the street you are turning into. What should you do?
choices: Go first, because your light is green
Honk so the pedestrian hurries
Wait for the pedestrian to finish crossing
Drive around the pedestrian
explanation:
When you turn, you must **yield to pedestrians crossing** the street you are turning into, even on a green light. **Wait until they are out of your path.**

**Wrong choices**
- Go first, because your light is green: Drivers who turn must yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk.
- Honk so the pedestrian hurries: Honking can scare the pedestrian. Just wait.
- Drive around the pedestrian: Driving around a pedestrian in a crosswalk is unsafe and illegal.

stem: You are driving out of a private driveway onto a public road. Who has the right of way?
choices: You, because you were there first
Only pedestrians, not cars
Whoever honks first
Traffic on the road and pedestrians on the sidewalk
oneLineConcept: Leaving a driveway: yield to everyone
explanation:
When entering a road from a **driveway, alley, or parking lot**, you must **yield to pedestrians on the sidewalk and to vehicles on the road**.

**Wrong choices**
- You, because you were there first: Leaving a driveway does not give you the right of way.
- Only pedestrians, not cars: You must yield to both pedestrians and vehicles.
- Whoever honks first: Honking does not give anyone the right of way.

stem: When making a right turn, where should your car be before you start the turn?
choices: In the center of the road
In the left lane
Close to the right side of the road
On the shoulder of the road
oneLineConcept: Right turn: start close to the right
explanation:
For a **right turn**, move **close to the right side of the road** (the right lane), signal at least 100 feet ahead, and **turn into the right lane** of the new road.

**Wrong choices**
- In the center of the road: Start a right turn from the right, not the center.
- In the left lane: Turning right from the left lane cuts across other traffic.
- On the shoulder of the road: Do not drive on the shoulder to make a turn.

stem: You are turning left from a two-way road onto another two-way road. Where should your car be before and after the turn?
choices: Start from the right lane; end in the far right lane
Start just right of the center line; end just right of the new road's center line
Start just right of the center line; end in the far left lane
Start in the oncoming lane; end in any open lane
oneLineConcept: Left turn two-way to two-way: stay right of center
explanation:
For a **left turn from a two-way road onto a two-way road**, start from the part of your lane **closest to the center line**. Finish the turn **to the right of the center line** of the new road.

**Wrong choices**
- Start from the right lane; end in the far right lane: Starting a left turn from the right lane cuts across traffic.
- Start just right of the center line; end in the far left lane: Ending on the left side puts you in the path of oncoming traffic.
- Start in the oncoming lane; end in any open lane: Never move into the oncoming lane to turn.

stem: Outside New York City, you are stopped at a steady red light and want to turn right. There is no sign. What may you do?
choices: Turn without stopping if no one is coming
You may never turn right on red
Turn after a full stop, yielding to pedestrians and traffic
Turn only if a green arrow also shows
oneLineConcept: Right on red outside NYC: full stop, then yield
explanation:
Outside New York City, you **may turn right on a steady red light** after a **full stop**, unless a sign prohibits it. You must **yield to pedestrians and other traffic** first.

**Wrong choices**
- Turn without stopping if no one is coming: You must come to a full stop first.
- You may never turn right on red: Outside NYC, right on red is allowed unless a sign prohibits it.
- Turn only if a green arrow also shows: A green arrow is not needed for right on red outside NYC.

stem: You are about to enter a roundabout. Whom must you yield to?
choices: Traffic already in the roundabout
Traffic waiting to enter behind you
No one, entering traffic has the right of way
Only large trucks in the roundabout
oneLineConcept: Roundabout: yield to traffic already inside
explanation:
When entering a **roundabout or traffic circle**, **yield to traffic already in it** and to pedestrians. Enter when there is a safe gap and drive **counterclockwise** (to the right of the center island).

**Wrong choices**
- Traffic waiting to enter behind you: Traffic behind you waits for you, not the other way around.
- No one, entering traffic has the right of way: Entering traffic must yield to vehicles already circling.
- Only large trucks in the roundabout: You must yield to all vehicles in the roundabout.

stem: You are at a T-intersection with no signs or signals. You are on the road that ends. Who has the right of way?
choices: You, because you are on the right
Whoever is going faster
Traffic on the through road
Whoever is turning left
explanation:
At a **T-intersection** with no signs or signals, drivers on the **road that ends must yield** to vehicles and pedestrians on the **through road**.

**Wrong choices**
- You, because you are on the right: The road that ends must yield, no matter which side.
- Whoever is going faster: Speed does not decide the right of way.
- Whoever is turning left: Turning left does not give anyone the right of way.

stem: You are in the intersection waiting to turn left. The light turns yellow and oncoming traffic stops. What should you do?
choices: Back up out of the intersection
Stay where you are until the next green light
Finish your turn when it is safe
Turn right instead
oneLineConcept: Already in intersection: complete the turn
explanation:
If you are **already in the intersection** when the light changes, **complete your turn when it is safe**. Do not back up or stay in the intersection blocking cross traffic.

**Wrong choices**
- Back up out of the intersection: Backing up in an intersection is dangerous.
- Stay where you are until the next green light: Waiting in the intersection blocks cross traffic.
- Turn right instead: Changing your turn suddenly is unsafe and confusing.

stem: You are driving through an intersection when you hear a siren and see an ambulance coming behind you. What should you do?
choices: Stop in the middle of the intersection
Back up out of the intersection
Drive through the intersection, then pull right and stop
Turn left in front of the ambulance
oneLineConcept: In an intersection: clear it, then pull over
explanation:
If an emergency vehicle comes while you are **in an intersection**, **continue through the intersection first**. Then **pull over to the right and stop** until it passes.

**Wrong choices**
- Stop in the middle of the intersection: Stopping in the intersection can block the ambulance and cross traffic.
- Back up out of the intersection: Backing up is dangerous and can cause a crash.
- Turn left in front of the ambulance: Turning across its path is dangerous.

stem: You are turning left from a one-way road onto another one-way road. Which lanes should you use?
choices: Start from the right lane and turn into the left lane
Start from the left lane and turn into the right lane
Start from the left lane and turn into the left lane
Start from the center lane and turn into any lane
oneLineConcept: One-way to one-way left turn: left lane to left lane
explanation:
For a **left turn from a one-way road onto a one-way road**, approach in the **far left lane** and turn into the **left lane** of the new road.

**Wrong choices**
- Start from the right lane and turn into the left lane: Starting from the right lane cuts across other traffic.
- Start from the left lane and turn into the right lane: Swinging wide into the right lane can hit vehicles in that lane.
- Start from the center lane and turn into any lane: You should use the left lane for a left turn.
